first.rationale: Aggressive competitor entry pricing creates an immediate SMB acquisition risk, and prior evidence indicates targeted pricing can lift acquisition and revenue in price-sensitive SMBs. A guarded, segment-targeted test is preferred because durable qualified revenue may be harmed if discount-acquired accounts have weaker retention or expansion. Verify the pricing record for downstream-quality evidence and the onboarding record because completion has also deteriorated and may represent the higher-value alternative.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening the onboarding flow. Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and the verified prior experiment improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Verified promotional pricing produced weaker 30-day retention and is therefore unsuitable as the primary response despite competitor pricing pressure. Measure qualified activation, retention, and early revenue by segment to confirm the prior result generalizes to current conditions.
